source_text:
Πάντες τε ἐταπεινοφρονεῖτε μηδὲν ἀλαζονευόμενοι, ὑποτασσόμενοι μᾶλλον ἦ ὑποτάσσοντες, ἥδιον διδόντες ἢ λαμβάνοντες. τοῖς ἐφοδίοις τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀρκούμενοι, καὶ προσέχοντες τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ ἐπιμελῶς ἐνεστερνισμένοι ἥτε τοῖς σπλάγχνοις, καὶ τὰ παθήματα αὐτοῦ ἦν πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν ὑμῶν.
οὕτως εἰρήνη βαθεῖα καὶ λιπαρὰ ἐδέδοτο πᾶσιν καὶ ἀκόρεστος πόθος εἰς ἀγαθοποιΐαν, καὶ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἔκχυσις ἐπὶ πάντας ἐγίνετο:
μεστοί τε ὁσίας βουλῆς, ἐν ἀγαθῇ προθυμίᾳ μετ’ εὐσεβοῦς πεποιθήσεως ἐξετείνετε τὰς χεῖρας ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν παντοκράτορα θεόν, ἱκετεύοντες αὐτὸν ἵλέως γενέσθαι, εἴ τι ἄκοντες ἡμάρτετε.
ἀγὼν ἦν ὑμῖν ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὑπὲρ πάσης τῆς ἀδελφότητος, εἰς τὸ σώζεσθαι μετ’ ἐλέους καὶ συνειδήσεως τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ.
εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀκέραιοι ἦτε καὶ ἀμνησίκακοι εἰς ἀλλήλους.
πᾶσα στάσις καὶ πᾶν σχίσμα βδελυκτὸν ἦν ὑμῖν. ἐπὶ τοῖς παραπτώμασιν τῶν πλησίον ἐπενθεῖτε: τὰ ὑστερήματα αὐτῶν ἴδια ἐκρίνετε.
ἀμεταμέλητοι ἦτε ἐπὶ πάσῃ ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ, ἕτοιμοι εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν.
τῇ παναρέτῳ καὶ σεβασμίῳ πολιτείᾳ κεκοσμημένοι πάντα ἐν τῷ φόβῳ αὐτοῦ ἐπετελεῖτε: τὰ προστάγματα καὶ τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ κυρίου ἐπὶ τὰ πλάτη τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν ἐγέγραπτο.
thought_title: The Corinthians' former humility and peace
orientation: The Roman church is recalling the Corinthians' former virtuous conduct before the faction arose.
pass_a_gloss: And you all were humble-minded, boasting in nothing, submitting rather than ruling, more gladly giving than receiving. Being content with the provisions of Christ, and attending to his words carefully, you had stored them in your inward parts, and his sufferings were before your eyes. Thus deep and rich peace had been given to all, and an insatiable longing for doing good, and a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit came upon all: and full of holy counsel, in good eagerness with devout confidence you stretched out your hands to the almighty God, beseeching him to be merciful, if in anything unwillingly you had sinned. A struggle was yours day and night on behalf of the whole brotherhood, so that the number of his elect might be saved with mercy and conscience. You were sincere and innocent and without memory of wrongs toward one another. Every faction and every division was abominable to you. Over the transgressions of your neighbors you mourned: their shortcomings you judged as your own. You were without regret in every good deed, ready for every good work. Adorned with the all-virtuous and reverend way of life, you accomplished all things in the fear of him: the commandments and the ordinances of the Lord were written on the tablets of your hearts.

lemmas.gloss: having stored in the inward parts

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'humility' for ταπεινοφροσύνη; the verbal form is rendered to match that root.
The glossary mandates 'submission' for ὑποταγή; the participle pair is rendered to preserve the contrast between being subject and subjecting others.

choices.english: you had stored them in your inward parts
choices.why: The verb means to take to heart or store within; 'inward parts' renders σπλάγχνοις literally as the seat of deep feeling.
rejected: you had treasured them in your hearts
you had embraced them in your bowels

choices.why: The compound means not remembering injuries; rendered literally to preserve the sense of holding no grudges.

bible_refs.note: τὰ προστάγματα καὶ τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ κυρίου ἐπὶ τὰ πλάτη τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν ἐγέγραπτο

pass_b_english: You were all humble-minded, with no trace of boasting. You submitted rather than ruled, and you were happier to give than to receive. You were content with the provisions of Christ, and you had stored his words carefully in your inward parts. His sufferings were before your eyes.
So a deep and rich peace was given to all, and an insatiable desire for doing good, and a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit came upon everyone.
Full of holy counsel, in good eagerness with reverent confidence, you stretched out your hands to God the Almighty, beseeching him to be merciful if you had sinned unwillingly.
It was a contest for you day and night on behalf of the whole brotherhood, so that the number of the elect of God might be saved with mercy and a good conscience.
You were sincere and innocent and without memory of wrongs toward one another.
Every faction and every division was abominable to you. You mourned over the transgressions of your neighbors; you judged their shortcomings to be your own.
You never regretted any act of doing good, ready for every good work.

Adorned with a wholly virtuous and reverent way of life, you accomplished everything in the fear of him. The commandments and the righteous requirements of the Lord were written on the broad places of your hearts.

polish.changed: Broke long clauses into shorter, clearer sentences; clarified the implied subject 'you' where needed; kept every claim and Scripture reference intact while making the rhythm more natural for reading aloud.

problems.why: Reader may not recognize these all refer to the same group.
Used interchangeably for people and groups; reader may wonder if 'the elect' is a distinct group from 'the elect of God'.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the elect of God' or clarify it refers to all believers.

edits.new: the number of the elect of God

fixed: The English already says 'his elect' where the source has 'τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ' (his elect), which is the same group as 'the elect of God'. The glossary entry for 'ἐκλεκτοί' is 'the elect', and 'his elect' is a natural possessive form of that. No change needed for the other instances, as they are not present in this passage.

last_rejected.why: εὐσεβοῦς = 'pious/reverent' is fine, but πεποιθήσεως means 'confidence/trust', not 'confidence that is reverent' — the phrase means 'with pious trust'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'reverent confidence' captures μετ' εὐσεβοῦς πεποιθήσεως accurately; 'pious trust' vs 'reverent confidence' is preference.

last_rejected.why: συνειδήσεως here means 'conscience' but the context implies a clear/good conscience; 'good conscience' adds 'good' not in source, but συνείδησις can carry this sense.
last_rejected.ruling: συνειδήσεως with positive context naturally implies 'good conscience'; no meaning changed.

last_rejected.quote: you judged their shortcomings to be your own
last_rejected.why: ἴδια ἐκρίνετε means 'you considered/judged their shortcomings as your own (ἴδια)'; 'to be your own' is a reasonable rendering of ἴδια.
last_rejected.ruling: 'to be your own' is standard rendering of ἴδια; claim actually supports the translation.
